verdict.rationale: AWS clearly ships both halves of the first-party IaC surface: CloudFormation templates provision the resources they describe, and the AWS CDK is a typed, multi-language construct framework that deploys through CloudFormation. However, the pack documents state and lifecycle semantics only thinly, through stack create/update/delete, and says nothing about rollback behavior. Missing for 10: documented rollback semantics (e.g. automatic rollback on failed updates), explicit state/drift management documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, infrastructure is code on day one — a first-party IaC surface (templates plus a typed CDK-style framework) with documented state/rollback semantics

citations.quote: You create a template that describes all the AWS resources that you want (like Amazon EC2 instances or Amazon RDS DB instances), and CloudFormation takes care of provisioning and configuring those resources for you.
The AWS CDK supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, C#/.Net, and Go. You can use any of these supported programming languages to define reusable cloud components known as constructs.
The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) is an open-source software development framework for defining cloud infrastructure in code and provisioning it through AWS CloudFormation.
Then, you deploy your CDK applications through AWS CloudFormation to provision or update your resources.
You can delete the stack just as easily, which deletes all the resources in the stack.
